title: The Sheriff Got (Very) Arrested…
description:

transcript.text: On December 8, 2021, around 2.35 a.m., Douglas County 911 Center received several 911 calls regarding a rollover crash on I-94 near Alexandria, Minnesota. The crash was near mile markers 107 or 108. One passer by noted that a man was now crawling down the shoulder of the highway. Multiple sheriff's deputies responded to the scene, as well as the Minnesota State Patrol, and noticed Good Samaritans trying to keep the crash survivor out of the freeway and helping purpose. provide aid. At the scene, they would find a man with obvious signs of intoxication, including slurred speech, poor balance, and odor of alcoholic beverage. However, unlike any call before, the man in question was the elected sheriff of the most populous county in Minnesota, Sheriff Hutchinson, commonly called Sheriff Hutch. What follows in this video is the documentation of their investigation that night and over the ensuing days. As their investigation progressed, The sheriff, Sheriff Hutch, made multiple false statements, including the outlandish claim that he had a cabbie, a cab driver, driving his squad vehicle at the time of the crash. The investigation also revealed that the sheriff was not wearing his seatbelt, and the squad car's black box reported a speed of 126 miles per hour in the moments prior to the crash. In total, Douglas County deputies and state troopers obtained more than 100 pieces of evidence as part of their investigation into the sheriff's behavior that night. including device forensic data from the black box, indicating how the car was being driven that night. At the request of the deputies, State Patrol took the primary role in this investigation. After photos were released of the squad vehicles condition by journalist Rebecca Bannon, Hennepin County officials requested an investigation of the journalist for alleged trespassing. The investigation came back unfounded. Sheriff Hutchinson refused to consent to the release of body-worn camera footage, preventing its release under Minnesota law. Sheriff Hutchinson refused to consent to a PBT and ultimately a search warrant was obtained for a urine sample. EMS personnel found the SUV's keys in the roadway and a deputy suspected Sheriff Hutch may have thrown the keys away so he would not be found in their possession.
